idea-plugin.name: Deadlock Lock-Order Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Builds a real lock acquisition-order graph from synchronized blocks/methods inside a single Java class, and flags a gutter warning on every site that closes a CYCLE in that graph -- the classic static-deadlock signal: one method acquires lock A then, while still holding it, acquires lock B; another method in the same class acquires B then A. If two threads hit those two methods at the same time, each can end up holding one lock while waiting forever for the other.

A real mechanism, not a text pattern -- this walks the actual PSI tree to find genuine lexical nesting of synchronized sites, builds a directed graph keyed by the lock expression text, and runs a real DFS cycle search over it (the textbook approach from MIT/ECOOP 2005 "Static Deadlock Detection for Java Libraries"). IntelliJ's own thread dumps only show a deadlock AFTER it happens at runtime; no Marketplace plugin found does static lock-order cycle detection ahead of time.

v0.2: cross-method edges. A lock acquired not by direct textual nesting but through a call to ANOTHER method of the same class -- synchronized(a) { helper(); } where helper() itself acquires lock b (directly, or transitively through its own calls) -- is now followed too, with real-cycle-safe memoization so a genuine call cycle between methods never hangs or crashes.

Stated honestly: still bounded to one class at a time -- it never resolves locks passed between different classes (including for the calls it follows), and matches lock identity by exact expression text (lockA and this.lockA are treated as different locks). Java only; ReentrantLock/java.util.concurrent locks and Kotlin's synchronized(){} are not yet covered.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
